key_insight: Boundary-layer detachment and breakdown of Prandtl scaling can coexist with numerical convergence to a smooth Euler flow as Reynolds number increases.
engineering_relevance: The findings caution against treating boundary-layer detachment alone as evidence that an inviscid approximation fails in the global energy norm.
method: Highly resolved direct numerical simulations of incompressible flow in a 2D periodic channel with no-slip walls.
Reynolds-dependent initial conditions with Prandtl-thickness boundary layers approaching a stationary analytic Euler flow.
Track velocity differences, energy dissipation, and detached-vortex structure as Reynolds number increases.
evidence_signal: Over the simulated interval, both the squared energy norm of the velocity difference and time-averaged energy dissipation scale approximately as Re^(-1/2), supporting convergence despite detachment.
watch_item: Evidence is numerical and limited to the simulated 2D configuration and time interval; it does not establish convergence for general wall-bounded flows.
paper_title: Boundary-layer detachment and infinite-Reynolds limit of two-dimensional wall-bounded flows
